text:
Ava (CEO): Thanks for a packed all-hands — use this thread for quick follow-ups on mission, positioning, competitors. Keep Qs short.

Meera (Product): Clarify: when we say 'unified runtime', should comms imply feature parity or just consistent API?

Rafael (CTO): Consistent API and core runtime primitives. Some ops/features will appear in Hosted first; parity is the goal but staggered cadence.

Jon (Eng): For Dedicated pilots: can we promise canary + rollback in the first delivery? Customer asked.

Rafael (CTO): Yes — canary + automatic rollback included in pilot. Private will follow after compatibility testing.

Priya (Growth): Sales request: one-line elevator for infra buyers that mentions governance + cost predictability.

Ava (CEO): Suggested: "Redwood delivers governed, production-grade inference with predictable unit economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Kai (Research): Competitor policy question: publish head-to-head or anonymized benchmarks?

Rafael (CTO): Publish reproducible, anonymized benchmarks plus methodology. Use customer case studies for context; avoid direct vendor callouts.

Meera (Product): Docs ask: can Product get a parity matrix + a short press blurb from leadership? Sales wants a 2-line battlecard too.

Ava (CEO): I'll drop a 2-paragraph press blurb and two-line sales hooks by EOD. Meera, Rafael: coordinate the parity matrix and batching impact table.

ops-bot: FYI maintenance tonight 22:30-23:00 UTC  nominal impact.

Priya (Growth): One last ask: for marketing, what reliability metrics are public? uptime feels thin.

Ava (CEO): Public: uptime and % requests meeting latency SLO. Internal/partner docs will include fallback rate and MTTx. We'll craft how to present those publicly.

Meera (Product): Great. Tagging @Rafael @Ava  I'll assemble assets and post here.

Ava (CEO): Thanks team, we'll close this after assets are live. :rocket:
